- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is weak (0.0–0.2) and forecast is consistently below true outcome, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias and increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% next period.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.2) and forecast is erratic, use 3-day moving average to smooth out noise before forecasting.
